Kept separate from the owner controller and the {@code Owner} model so the 24 * rule for deciding when two owners denote the same person lives in one place, as pure functions 25 * with no web or persistence dependencies. Mirrors {@link TelephoneNormalizer}, 26 * {@link EmailNormalizer} and {@link HouseholdNormalizer}, whose comparison keys it composes. 27 * 28 *

The key is the owner's normalized telephone, email (or the empty string when absent) and 29 * household id joined with {@code '|'} separators: 30 * {@code normalizedTelephone + '|' + email + '|' + householdId}. Two owners are the same, and a 31 * create is rejected as a {@code 409 Conflict}, only when their whole keys are equal — so the 32 * previously separate telephone, email and household duplicate checks are all subsumed by this one 33 * key. Because the telephone is part of the key, two members of the same household (same 34 * {@code householdId}) with different telephones have different keys and are both allowed; only an 35 * exact full-key match is a duplicate. 36 */ 37 public abstract class OwnerIdentity { 38 39 /** Separates the telephone, email and household components of the key. */ 40 private static final String SEPARATOR = "|"; 41 42 /** 43 * Builds the identity key from an owner's raw parts. The telephone and email are reduced to 44 * their {@linkplain TelephoneNormalizer#toComparisonKey comparison} / 45 * {@linkplain EmailNormalizer#toComparisonKey comparison} forms so values stored in different 46 * shapes still compose equal keys; an absent (null or blank) email contributes the empty string, 47 * and an absent household id likewise contributes the empty string. 48 * 49 * @param telephone the owner's telephone (normalized on create), or null 50 * @param email the owner's email (lower-cased on create), or null/blank when absent 51 * @param householdId the owner's household id, or null 52 * @return the owner's identity key 53 */ 54 public static String identityKey(String telephone, String email, String householdId) { 55 String telephonePart = telephone == null ? "" : TelephoneNormalizer.toComparisonKey(telephone); 56 String emailPart = (email == null || email.isBlank()) ? "" : EmailNormalizer.toComparisonKey(email); 57 String householdPart = householdId == null ? "" : householdId; 58 return telephonePart + SEPARATOR + emailPart + SEPARATOR + householdPart; 59 } 60 61 /** 62 * Builds the identity key from a persisted owner's stored telephone, email and household id. 63 * 64 * @param owner the owner (non-null) 65 * @return the owner's identity key 66 */ 67 public static String identityKey(Owner owner) { 68 return identityKey(owner.getTelephone(), owner.getEmail(), owner.getHouseholdId()); 69 } 70 71 } 72

file.content:
description: >-
            The optional 4-digit postcode of the pet owner. When present it must be
            valid for the owner's city per a fixed table keyed by the city's region
            ('Sydney' -> NSW 2000-2099, 'Melbourne' -> VIC 3000-3099, 'Brisbane' ->
            QLD 4000-4099). A city with no known region accepts any 4-digit postcode.
            A postcode that is malformed or out of range for the city's region is
            rejected with a 400. Stored and returned when given.
          type: string
          pattern: "^[0-9]{4}$"
          example: '2000'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            When omitted on create it defaults to the server's current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: >-
            The optional date of birth of the pet owner, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD'
            format. When present it is used to derive the owner's 'ageBand'.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Optional create-time directive. When true, the owner is permitted to
            share a household with an existing owner, so the create request is not
            rejected as a household duplicate even when another owner has the same
            last name and address (compared case-insensitively with collapsed
            whitespace).
          type: boolean
          example: true
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            locality:
              title: Locality
              description: >-
                The owner's locality (region), derived by preferring the postcode: a 4-digit
                postcode within a known region's range ('NSW' 2000-2099, 'VIC' 3000-3099,
                'QLD' 4000-4099) yields that region. When the postcode is absent or in no known
                range, it falls back to a fixed city-to-region table ('Sydney' -> 'NSW',
                'Melbourne' -> 'VIC', 'Brisbane' -> 'QLD'). A city not in the table with no
                region-bearing postcode derives the locality 'UNKNOWN'.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                The owner's customer code, formatted '<LAST3>-<NNNN>' where LAST3 is the
                upper-cased first three letters of lastName and NNNN is a global 4-digit
                zero-padded sequence equal to one more than the number of owners at the
                time the owner was created.
              type: string
              example: 'SMI-0007'
              readOnly: true
            checkDigit:
              title: Check digit
              description: >-
                A single Luhn check digit (0-9) computed over the digits contained in the
                customerCode.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              maximum: 9
              example: 4
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: >-
                The owner's membership number, formatted '<customerCode>-M<YY>' where
                YY is the last two digits of the registrationDate year.
              type: string
              example: 'SMI-0007-M26'
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: >-
                A stable identifier shared by every owner in the same household - those with
                the same last name and address, compared case-insensitively with collapsed
                whitespace. Owners who opt in with 'sharesHousehold' to join an existing
                household receive that household's identifier.
              type: string
              example: 'a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9012345678901234567890abcdef123456'
              readOnly: true
            identityKey:
              title: Identity key
              description: >-
                The owner's derived duplicate-detection key, formed by joining the normalized
                telephone, the email (or an empty string when absent) and the householdId with
                '|' separators (normalizedTelephone + '|' + email + '|' + householdId). A create
                is rejected as a duplicate only when this whole key equals that of an existing
                owner.
              type: string
              example: '+61412345678|george.franklin@example.com|a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f9012345678901234567890abcdef123456'

The build compiles cleanly and the test fails with the **exact same** expected/actual hash values (`29a5e2…` vs `98b306…`) as it did before my changes — confirming the refactor is purely structural and preserves behaviour byte-for-byte. The test remains red only because it asserts the *upcoming* change's behaviour (deterministic household id from lastName+postcode), which I was told not to implement.

## What I did

I prepared the code so the upcoming change lands as a small, localized diff, in the codebase's own idioms — without implementing it.

**`OwnerRestControllerV1` — two behaviour-preserving extractions:**

1. **`householdIdFor(OwnerFieldsDto)`** — both `addOwner` and `updateOwner` inlined `HouseholdNormalizer.toHouseholdId(lastName, address)`. They now route through one helper, so the decision of *which fields key the household* lives in a single place. When the change flips `address → postcode`, it edits one method instead of two call sites that could drift. (In `updateOwner` this is exactly equivalent: it derived from `currentOwner`'s just-copied `lastName`/`address`, which are verbatim the DTO's.)

2. **`markPossibleDuplicate(Owner)`** — the `find + set possibleDuplicate + set possibleDuplicateOf` trio in `addOwner` is now one named method. This is the natural home for the change's new rule that *a declared household member is not a suspected duplicate* — the suppression drops into one place rather than tangling `addOwner`'s inline field-stamping.

## What I deliberately did *not* touch, and why

- **`HouseholdNormalizer.toHouseholdId`** — every restructure it needs (separator `\n`→`|`, field `address`→`postcode`, output full-lowercase→12-char-uppercase) *is* a behaviour change, so there's no safe prep. The template for the new shape already exists in the codebase: `CustomerCode.hash8` does precisely "first N upper-hex of SHA-256 over composed parts" with `SEPARATOR`/`HASH_LENGTH` constants. The change author can mirror it directly.
- **`DuplicateHouseholdException` / `rejectHouseholdDuplicate`** — creating these now would be dead code and would be implementing the change. The seam is already in place: `DuplicateOwnerException` is an extensible base and `ExceptionControllerAdvice` handles the whole family through one `@ExceptionHandler(DuplicateOwnerException.class)`, so the new 409 subtype (carrying `householdId`, exactly as `DuplicateOwnerIdentityException` carries `identityKey`) needs no new handler.
